messages:
tara_support: FYI flagged by ACME support rep — customer says responses got 'snappier' and cut out the usual elaboration after the model bump to rdx-4.2. They included side-by-side examples. Can someone triage? :eyes:

michael_cs: thanks — can you paste the exact request IDs or the example pairs? also which endpoint (chat vs completions)?

tara_support: Here are the examples they pasted (redacted customer data). Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions, model switched from rdx-4.1 to rdx-4.2 last week.

----BEGIN CUSTOMER EXAMPLES----
Prompt: "Summarize the security considerations for storing API keys in a web app."

BEFORE (rdx-4.1):
- Keep keys on the server, never in client JS.
- Use environment variables and KMS for rotation.
- Limit scopes and use short-lived tokens when possible.
- Log access, monitor anomalies, rotate keys on suspected compromise.

AFTER (rdx-4.2):
- Store keys server-side and rotate regularly.

Customer note: "The after reply is accurate but much more terse and feels brusque to our end users. We've had a few support tickets complaining response tone changed (less guidance)."
----END CUSTOMER EXAMPLES----

michael_cs: that's helpful. do we have request IDs? if the customer has them ask for request_id, timestamp, and candidate_id. otherwise we can repro with their prompt.

tara_support: they gave a sample request id: req_8f3b2a (from last Thu). also included a minimal repro: same prompt with system message: "You are a helpful assistant that explains security best practices."

matt_eng: assigning myself. quick q: is this strictly verbosity reduction or also factual differences?

tara_support: mostly verbosity/tone. content coverage is still correct but missing actionable bullets and examples. they call it 'loss of helpfulness'.

matt_eng: kk. likely regression in the default verbosity/penalization for verbosity change or a decode param tweak. two immediate checks: 1) verify server rollout timeline and config for rdx-4.2 (temperature, max_tokens, top_p, penalize settings) 2) reproduce locally with exact payload.

oncall_bot: @matt_eng acknowledged — created incident INC-2027-73 (priority: P3) to track customer regression report.

michael_cs: repro steps I tried just now (from my laptop):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{\n    "model":"rdx-4.2",\n    "messages":[\n      {"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant that explains security best practices."},\n      {"role":"user","content":"Summarize the security considerations for storing API keys in a web app."}\n    ],\n    "max_tokens":150\n  }'
```

michael_cs: output I got is short, matches customer's AFTER example. reran with model rdx-4.1 and got longer, enumerated bullets.

sre-bot: note: observed config change rolled 2027-11-02 03:12 UTC for rdx-4.2 instances: default max_tokens for chat was trimmed from 512 to 150 for some runtime tags.

matt_eng: that explains part of it — max_tokens trim would shorten outputs, but doesn't fully account for style change (lost bullets). next: check decode/response-formatting defaults and any system prompt modifications in the rollout. also check if any new sanitization / response-compaction policy applied.

tara_support: customer is asking for timeline and ETA to fix — can we give them a repro and mitigation they can use while we investigate?

michael_cs: mitigation: set explicit max_tokens to 300 and include a user/system instruction to request bullets, e.g., add to system: "Always include 3-5 actionable bullet points and an example." ask customer to pin model to rdx-4.1 if they need immediate stable behavior.

matt_eng: agreed. I'll reproduce at scale and run an A/B with traffic pinned to 4.1 vs 4.2 with identical decode params. action items: 
- matt_eng: verify rollout config diffs (decode params, system prompt changes) — ETA 4h
- michael_cs: send repro command + customer req_id to logs team and confirm request storage — ETA 1h
- tara_support: share mitigation instructions to customer and offer to pin them to rdx-4.1 for 48h — ETA 30m

tara_support: sending mitigation now. :white_check_mark: I'll update the ticket when customer responds.

matt_eng: quick note: if rollout accidentally changed default system-content or added a compacting post-process, we should flag as rollback candidate. tagging @michael_cs for any logs with req_8f3b2a.

michael_cs: got it. attaching the customer's original request metadata and raw response bodies to INC-2027-73.

sre-bot: deployment mark: rollback allowed window open for the next 6 hours.

matt_eng: thanks. I'll post findings in the incident thread once I compare sample outputs and kernel/runtime config. initial hypothesis: default max_tokens + a new response compacting heuristic combined to reduce verbosity; we'll confirm if it was intentional policy.

tara_support: customer appreciated the quick mitigation steps. will keep thread updated. :pray:
